To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified three new alleles of the human IGHG gene, IGHG2, that are polymorphic and have different prevalence among different populations.

we have found three new alleles of the IGHG2 locus, which we have characterized by sequencing and by a complete sequence specific typing system, and we have determined the allele prevalence among Danish Caucasians, Japanese, and Mozambican Blacks.

we have discovered three new IGHG2 alleles (IGHG*03, *04, and *05), that we have developed a sequence-specific PCR typing system for the different IGHG2 allotypes, that we have identified the polymorphic residues in IGHG2, that we have found that the IGHG2 allele frequencies differ among the three populations studied, and that we have identified an IGHG2 polymorphism that probably is a result of gene conversion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new alleles of human IGHG and their distribution in various populations.
the genetic diversity of IGHG genes and the impact of genetic variation on human health.
the genetic basis for the differences in antibody response to polysaccharides and other antigens between individuals and ethnic groups.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are four alleles of IGH G2 in Caucasians (G2m(n+), G2m(n-), IGHG2 *03 and IGH G2*04) and two alleles in Mozambicans and Japanese (G2m (n+) and IGHG 2*03).
the G2m allotype polymorphism is a complex phenomenon with multiple allotypes and alleles.

IGHG2 encodes four different allotypes of the human IgG2 molecule, G2m(n-), G2m(n+) (encoded by IGHG*02), G2m(+) (encoded by the new IGHG2 allele 05), and G2m(ny) (encoded by IGVHG2*04), the last two being isoallotypes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IGHG2 is polymorphic and that the IGHG2 alleles differ in the frequency of their expression in different populations.
the G2m(allotype) n- allele is present in 99.6% of Japanese, 98.5% of Mozambicans, and 95.5% of Danish Caucasians.
the G2m(allotypes) of the human IgG2 heavy chain are encoded by three alleles, IGHG2 *01, *02, and *04, which are present in different ethnic groups with different prevalence.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the IGHG2 locus is polymorphic in all ethnic groups studied, that the IGH locus is highly polymorphic in all three ethnic groups studied, and that the polymorphism in the IGH locus has a significant impact on the level of serum IgG2.
the G2m(allotypes) are not only polymorphic, but also show considerable ethnic diversity, and that the G2M(n-) allotype is the most prevalent in Danish Caucasians.
IGHG2 is highly polymorphic in the CH1 domain.
